summary: Every word in the selected range can independently change the result, so inspecting its endpoints is necessary and the linear scan already matches the lower bound.

optimality.argument: For each of the k = right - left + 1 selected words, changing an unread first or last character can change whether that word contributes. A correct algorithm must therefore inspect endpoint information from every selected word in the worst case, while the reference performs constant work for each one.

replacement_checks.evidence: An adversary can make any uninspected selected word the only vowel string by changing its first and last characters, establishing Omega(k) required inspections.
The reference visits exactly k selected words and performs two constant-time membership checks per word, using only fixed vowel data and a counter.

Authored cases cover one-character words, all five vowels, both one-sided failures, inclusive boundaries, ignored outside words, middle ranges, and maximum word length; exhaustive endpoint classifications were also compared with a direct oracle.
